summary: 100-foot steel stair tower, probably built by a CCC crew in 1937 near Jay Cooke State Park; county survey list marks it removed; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 100-foot Aermotor stairway tower of steel with four legs (1952 survey note)
facts.status_note: The county survey list marks the tower removed and firelookout.org lists it as gone. No source read describes the site now.
facts.agency: Minnesota Forest Service (owner in the county survey list)

access.note: Tower site is along what is now Jay Cooke Road; the Forest Lookouts page files it under Jay Cooke State Park, a Minnesota state park. No source describes access to the former tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1937 Big Lake Breeze item and the county table say 100 feet; the 1952 survey note says about 115 feet. Both are reported in the story.

notes_for_editor: Built year, design and removal are supported by two sources (weebly page quoting the 1937 CCC-era item, and the county survey list). The county list does not give a removal date; the 1952 survey note is followed by Removed, so the year of removal is unknown and no removal event is recorded. Height conflict: 100 ft (1937 item, county table) vs about 115 ft (1952 survey note). No staffing or fire history found. Site today: no source read describes what remains. Only the Carlton County PDF and the Forest Lookouts page were used for the tower itself.
